points.description: States the circumstance: multiple hidden layers are desirable when the task needs deep (hierarchical) learning or extraction of complex features that a single hidden layer cannot learn efficiently. Equivalent wording such as 'when the problem requires learning more complex/abstract features' earns the mark.

Gives a valid example of such a situation, such as multiclass classification or the XOR function (or another task needing complex feature learning). One correct example is enough. Vague examples such as 'complex problems' do not earn the mark.

rubric.notes: Full marks (2) for stating that multiple hidden layers are needed when the task requires deep or complex feature learning, plus one valid example such as multiclass classification or XOR. Award 1 mark for the circumstance alone or for a valid example given without the feature-learning reason; award 0 for generic answers such as 'when the problem is hard' with no link to feature learning. Equivalent wording and other correct examples earn the marks.
